set.prevailing_wage_basis: HOME: 24 CFR 92.354(a) requires Davis-Bacon wages on construction contracts for housing with 12 or more HOME-assisted units (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354). CDBG: Davis-Bacon applies to residential projects of 8 or more units under HCDA Section 110 and 24 CFR 570.603.
set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check: December 5, 2024 HRC memo confirms 65 percent CDBG capital minimum, direct allocation of capital and HOME funds as loans, biennial public services NOFA, $171,000 General Fund under Council Policy A-8, HOME for low and very low income, and HRC Feb/Mar, Council April, HUD May 15 timing. FY 2024-25 allocations were $604,684 CDBG and $237,782 HOME. The 2025 project examples (Paulson Park, Lot 12) are not in this memo. Capital funds are allocated directly, not through an annual capital NOFA.

reason: Memo matches on capital share, AMI, cycle and timing; added HOME and CDBG prevailing wage basis.

set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check: January 9, 2023 staff report confirms 2015 expansion, over $47 million collected, $11 and $22 per square foot office/R&D recommendation, CPI indexing, and the $13 legacy versus $19.50 rate; January 24, 2023 Council minutes confirm adoption of $11 and $22 (7-0) after a failed $11.50/$23 amendment. 2024 HHSC report confirms 55-year lower income restriction and the $16 million 2022 NOFA; Council matter 24-0863 confirms $29,533,000 in 2024. The $18 million 2026 NOFA figure was not found in Legistar titles. prevailing_wage_trigger true has no cited rule; no Sunnyvale NOFA prevailing wage requirement was found, so the only apparent basis is Labor Code 1720(b) for funded projects, which under Tier 3 rules would be unclear.

reason: Fee rates, collections, affordability term and 2024 award match the staff report, Council minutes and NOFA reports.

set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check: fund page confirms Cisco $50 million (2018) and Apple $50 million (2019), over $96 million invested, no or low interest acquisition and predevelopment financing for 42 ELI and supportive developments with more than 4,100 units, capacity grants to 8 developers (1,600 units) and to Campbell, Morgan Hill, Mountain View and San Jose. Open Funding Opportunities page says funding is by RFP or invitation. prevailing_wage_trigger false has no cited rule; private philanthropic funds are not public funds, but no ruling on point was opened.

reason: Fund page matches on investment totals, terms, focus on ELI and supportive housing, and RFP or invitation process.
